_about: Device setup paths. Every instruction is checked against the emulator's own site (listed per device in `sources`) or, for mGBA on macOS, the installed app. Nothing here names a download location for the game itself.
terms: An app that plays Game Boy Advance games on your computer. mGBA is the one this guide uses.
Project Blonde itself: one file ending in .gba. You may see it called a ROM.
Your progress: a small file ending in .sav that sits beside the game file.
A snapshot the emulator takes of the exact moment. Handy, but not the same as saving your game — see step 5.

devices.name: iPhone & iPad
devices.emulator_note: a free emulator by Testut Tech on the App Store.
quick: Save the Project Blonde .gba file to the Files app.
In Delta tap +, choose Files, and pick the game.
Play. Save from the game’s own START menu.

p: Open the App Store, search for Delta – Game Emulator by Testut Tech and install it. It is free.
In the European Union, Delta is distributed through AltStore PAL (altstore.io) rather than the App Store.
note: Delta plays several classic systems. Project Blonde is a Game Boy Advance game and needs no extra files or BIOS.

steps.t: Put the game file on your device
p: Get the Project Blonde .gba file onto your iPhone or iPad: download it in Safari, AirDrop it from a computer, or copy it into iCloud Drive. It lands in the Files app, usually under Downloads.
Delta imports .gba files. If your download is a .zip, tap it once in Files to unpack it first.
Open Delta and tap the + button in the top-right corner of the main screen. Choose Files, find the game and tap it.
Project Blonde appears on the Game Boy Advance page of your library. Tap it to play.
Delta shows an on-screen Game Boy Advance. Bluetooth controllers (PlayStation, Xbox, Switch and MFi) work once paired in iOS Settings.
START opens the game’s menu; in battle, START on the FIGHT menu is also how you Mega Evolve.
Save from inside the game: press START and choose SAVE, exactly as on a real Game Boy Advance. This writes your save file, the one that moves to another device or a newer version of the game.
Delta also has save states in its pause menu. They are a convenience that lives inside Delta; never rely on one as your only save.
Export: in the library, touch and hold Project Blonde and choose Export Save File. Save the .sav file to Files or iCloud Drive.
Restore or move in: touch and hold the game and choose Import Save File, then pick a .sav file.

Automatic backup: in Delta’s Settings open Delta Sync, tap Service and sign in to Google Drive or Dropbox. Delta then backs up your games and save files and restores them on another iPhone or iPad signed in to the same account.
note: Bringing a save from a computer

mGBA writes saves that are 16 bytes longer than Delta expects (it appends clock data). A save made in mGBA must be trimmed to exactly 131,072 bytes before Delta will load it; a save exported from Delta opens in mGBA as it is. This was measured in the project’s own tests.

problems: I can’t find the game in the Files picker
It is usually in On My iPhone → Downloads or iCloud Drive → Downloads. If you see a .zip, tap it in the Files app first to unpack it.
My imported save doesn’t load
Delta only accepts a Game Boy Advance save of exactly 131,072 bytes. Saves written by mGBA are 131,088 bytes and must be trimmed. Saves exported from Delta are already the right size.
The clock in the game is wrong
Delta gives the game your device’s local time. Set the in-game clock at any Pokémon Center.
Can I link with a friend on Delta?

This guide has no verified way to use Project Blonde’s cable link on Delta. Delta’s documented multiplayer is local play for some home-console systems and online play for Nintendo DS games. See Link Play on the Play page.

devices.name: Android
devices.emulator_note: a free, open-source front end that runs the mGBA emulator as a ‘core’.
quick: Load Content and pick the Project Blonde .gba file.
Play. Save from the game’s own START menu.

p: mGBA, the emulator this guide uses on computers, has no official Android app: its developers say so on their own site. RetroArch is an official, free, open-source app that runs the same mGBA emulator as a ‘core’, so the game behaves the same as on a computer.
There are many other Game Boy Advance emulators on Google Play. This guide has not tested Project Blonde on them and does not recommend one by name.
Go to retroarch.com, open Platforms and download the Android version, or install it from F-Droid, the Samsung Galaxy Store or the Amazon Appstore.
RetroArch’s own site says the Google Play version is out of date and recommends the download from its site or another store.
note: If you download the .apk from retroarch.com, Android asks you to allow your browser to install apps. That prompt is expected for apps from outside Google Play.

p: Open RetroArch. Choose Load Core → Download a Core and pick Nintendo – Game Boy Advance (mGBA).
A core is the part of RetroArch that knows how to be one particular console. You only do this once.
Put the .gba file somewhere easy to find, such as your Download folder. In RetroArch choose Load Content, browse to the file and select it. If asked which core to use, choose mGBA.
The mGBA core loads .gba files directly.
Save from inside the game: press START and choose SAVE, exactly as on a real Game Boy Advance. This writes your save file, the one that moves to another device or a newer version of the game.
RetroArch also offers save states in its Quick Menu. They only work in RetroArch with the same core; treat them as a convenience.

With the mGBA core, your in-game save is a file ending in .srm with the same name as the game, kept in RetroArch’s Save directory. You can see or change that folder under Settings → Directory → Save Files.
Copy the .srm file somewhere safe with a file manager, and always before you update the game. It holds the same battery-save data that mGBA on a computer stores as .sav.
note: RetroArch writes the save file when you close the content or quit from its menu. Use Quick Menu → Close Content before swiping the app away.

problems: RetroArch can’t see my files
Grant it storage permission when asked, and keep the game in a normal folder such as Download rather than inside another app’s private storage.
There’s no mGBA in the list
Use Load Core → Download a Core first. If the list is empty, check your internet connection and try Online Updater → Update Core Info Files.
My progress vanished after an update
The save is matched by file name. Give the new .gba the same name as the old one, or rename the .srm to match the new file.
Can I link with a friend on Android?
The mGBA core in RetroArch does not support netplay or the link cable, according to its own documentation. This guide has no verified link setup on Android.
alternatives: Other Android emulators exist, including paid and free apps on Google Play. They were not tested with Project Blonde for this guide.

devices.name: Windows
devices.emulator_note: a free, open-source Game Boy Advance emulator.
devices.requires: a Windows PC (64-bit or 32-bit builds are offered)
quick: Open Project Blonde with File → Load ROM…
Play. Save from the game’s own START menu.
Keep a copy of the .sav file somewhere safe.

p: Go to the official site, mgba.io, and open Downloads. Under Windows choose the 64-bit installer, or the portable archive if you would rather not install anything.
Run the installer, or unpack the archive into a folder of its own.
Make a folder for Project Blonde, in Documents for example, and move the .gba file into it.
Do not keep the game inside Program Files. mGBA’s own FAQ warns that Windows redirects saves written there to a hidden folder, which makes them hard to find.
In mGBA choose File → Load ROM…, find the game and open it. The title screen appears straight away; no extra files are needed.
Open Tools → Settings…. Keyboard lets you choose a key for each button; Controllers does the same for a gamepad.
Save from inside the game: press START and choose SAVE, exactly as on a real Game Boy Advance. This writes your save file, the one that moves to another device or a newer version of the game.
mGBA can also take save states (File → Save State, or Quick save). They are useful before a hard battle, but they only work in mGBA. Treat them as a convenience, never as your only save.
Next to the game is a file with the same name ending in .sav. Copy it somewhere safe from time to time, and always before you update the game or change device.
If you move where saves go, the setting is under Tools → Settings… → Paths.

problems: The game opens but my progress is gone
mGBA looks for a .sav with exactly the same name as the game file, in the same folder. If you renamed or moved one of them, put them back together with matching names.
I can’t find my save file
If the game is inside Program Files, Windows may have redirected the save to %LocalAppData%\VirtualStore. Move the game to Documents.

devices.name: macOS
quick: Open Project Blonde with File → Load ROM…
Play. Save from the game's own menu.
Keep a copy of the .sav file somewhere safe.

p: Go to the official mGBA site, mgba.io, and open Downloads. Choose macOS (modern, 10.13+).
Open the file you downloaded and drag mGBA into your Applications folder.
note: The first time you open it
macOS may ask you to confirm that you want to open an app downloaded from the internet. That is expected for apps from outside the App Store.

p: Make a folder for Project Blonde — in Documents, for example — and move the game file into it.
mGBA keeps your save in the same folder as the game, so choose a place you won't tidy away later.
In mGBA, choose File → Load ROM…, find the game file and open it. The title screen appears straight away; you don't need any extra files.
Open Tools → Settings…. Keyboard lets you choose a key for each button; Controllers does the same for a gamepad.
For a bigger picture, use Audio/Video → Toggle fullscreen.
Save from inside the game: press START and choose SAVE, exactly as on a real Game Boy Advance. This writes your save file, the one that moves to another device or a newer version of the game.
mGBA can also take save states (File → Save State, or Quick save). They are useful before a hard battle, but they only work in mGBA. Treat them as a convenience, never as your only save.
Look in your Project Blonde folder: next to the game is a file with the same name ending in .sav. Copy it somewhere safe from time to time — and always before you update the game or switch device.
If you ever change where saves go, the setting is under Tools → Settings… → Paths, in the Save games row. The default is the same folder as the game.

problems: The game opens but my progress is gone
mGBA looks for a .sav with exactly the same name as the game file, in the same folder. If you renamed or moved one of them, put them back together with matching names.
A button does nothing, or the character walks on its own
In Tools → Settings… → Controllers, click each direction's box and clear both the analog and the button entry, then set it again.

save.title: In-game save or save state?
save.lead: They sound alike and behave very differently. Only one of them is your adventure.
rows: Moves between devices and game updates.
Use this. It is your adventure.
Usually stays on that device and emulator.
A convenience. Never your only copy.

topics.label: Back up
topics.title: Back up your save
text: Your progress is one small file. Copy it before you update the game, change emulator or change device.
mGBA (Windows, macOS): the .sav file beside the game. Delta: touch and hold the game → Export Save File, or switch on Delta Sync. RetroArch: the .srm file in its Save directory.

topics.label: Restore
topics.title: Restoring a save
text: Put the backed-up file back where the emulator looks for it, with the same name as the game: beside the .gba for mGBA, through Import Save File in Delta, or in the Save directory (as .srm) for RetroArch.
Save states cannot be restored into a different emulator, and may not survive a game update. The in-game save can.

topics.label: Move
topics.title: Moving between devices
text: The in-game save is the same battery-save data everywhere; only the file name and length differ.

Delta → computer: export the save and place it beside the game as game name.sav. Computer → Delta: mGBA’s save is 16 bytes longer than Delta accepts and must be trimmed to 131,072 bytes first. RetroArch (mGBA core): uses the extension .srm for the same data.

topics.label: Link Play
topics.title: Link Play
text: Two copies of Project Blonde with the same link version, PB-LINK-0001, can trade (including trade evolutions), fight Single and Double Battles, and both Mega Evolve. Other games and other link versions are refused. Record Mixing and the Union Room are not supported.

Verified setup: two mGBA instances on one computer. Open the game, then choose File → New multiplayer window and load the game in the second window with its own save file. Both players talk to the link receptionist in a Pokémon Center.
Not verified: Delta, RetroArch on Android, and play over the internet. The RetroArch mGBA core does not support the link cable. This guide makes no claim that those work.

trouble: The game doesn’t appear in my emulator

Emulators list a game only after you open or import it. mGBA: File → Load ROM… and browse to the file. Delta: tap + and choose Files; it then sits on the Game Boy Advance page. RetroArch: Load Content, then browse. If the file cannot be picked, it is probably still zipped or has the wrong ending.
The file has the wrong ending

The game must end in .gba, not .zip, .gba.zip or .gba.txt. Unpack a .zip first. A save ends in .sav (mGBA, Delta) or .srm (RetroArch). Computers hide file endings by default: on Windows switch on File name extensions in File Explorer’s View menu; on a Mac tick Show all filename extensions in Finder’s Advanced settings.
The patch won’t apply, or the patched game won’t start

A patch fits exactly one base game. If the patching tool reports a checksum mismatch, your base file is a different release or revision, or has already been modified; use an untouched copy of the base game named under Current release. After patching, compare your file’s SHA-256 with the one published on this page.
The game shows a white or black screen
Check that the file ends in .gba and is the full 32 MB. A partly downloaded or still-zipped file will not start.
Continue is missing from the title menu
The emulator did not find your save. It is matched by file name: the save must have the same name as the game file and be where that emulator expects it.
How do I check the SHA-256 checksum?

Windows: in PowerShell run Get-FileHash followed by the file’s path. macOS: in Terminal run shasum -a 256 followed by the file’s path. The result must match the checksum under Current release exactly.
There is no sound

Check the device volume first. iPhone: the silent switch can mute Delta; Delta’s Settings has a Respect Silent Mode switch. mGBA: see that Audio/Video → Mute is not ticked. RetroArch: see that Settings → Audio → Mute is off.
Delta: I can’t import my save

In Delta the + button imports games only. A save goes in through the game itself: touch and hold Project Blonde in the library and choose Import Save File. The file must be a .sav of exactly 131,072 bytes; one written by mGBA is 16 bytes longer and has to be trimmed first.
I updated and my progress is gone

Nothing is lost while you have the save file. The new game simply has not been given it: follow the update steps for your device. If the new version shows a damaged or empty save, do not save over it; go back to the old version with your backup.
The in-game clock is wrong or stuck
Set it at any Pokémon Center; there is no penalty. The game reads the clock from your device through the emulator.
A save state stopped working after I updated
Save states belong to one emulator and one game version. Use your in-game save, which carries over.
The game says the link partner is incompatible
Both players need the same Project Blonde version (link version PB-LINK-0001), and for battles the same battle options.
I walked into Viridian Forest and the game froze
That was a bug in build v100, fixed in v101. Update the game; your save is unaffected.
Rocks in Hoenn won’t smash
A bug in builds v100 and v101, fixed in v102.
A grunt blocks the Space Center stairs again
Fixed in v103. On an older build, leave the building and walk back in.

update.title: How to Update Project Blonde Without Losing Your Save
update.lead: A new version is a new game file. Your progress is a separate save file, so updating means: back the save up, put the new game in place, and hand the save to it.
rules: Press START and choose SAVE. Only this in-game save moves to a new version. A save state is tied to one emulator and one game version and may not load after an update.
Back up before you touch anything
Copy the save file somewhere else and leave that copy alone. It is your way back.
Do not delete the old version until you have checked the new one.

devices.name: iPhone & iPad
steps: Open Project Blonde in Delta, press START and choose SAVE. Return to Delta’s library.
Back up: touch and hold Project Blonde and choose Export Save File. Save the .sav file to the Files app or iCloud Drive.
Get the new version from Get the game on this page. If it comes as a patch, apply it to your base game as described there, so that you end up with a new .gba file. Save it to the Files app.
In Delta tap +, choose Files and pick the new .gba. Delta adds it as a second game and leaves the old one where it is. If both show the same name, touch and hold one and choose Rename.
Restore: touch and hold the new game, choose Import Save File and pick the .sav you exported in step 2.
Open the new game and choose Continue.

devices.name: Android
steps: In the game press START and choose SAVE. Then open RetroArch’s Quick Menu and choose Close Content, which writes the save file.
Back up: with a file manager, open RetroArch’s Save folder (shown under Settings → Directory → Save Files) and copy the file ending in .srm that has the game’s name to another folder.

Get the new version from Get the game on this page. If it comes as a patch, apply it to your base game as described there, so that you end up with a new .gba file. Put it in the folder where you keep the game.
Restore: RetroArch matches the save by name. If the new game file has a different name, make a copy of the .srm in the Save folder and rename the copy to the new game’s name, keeping .srm at the end.
Choose Load Content, pick the new .gba and choose the mGBA core if asked.
On the title menu choose Continue.

devices.name: Windows
steps: In the game press START and choose SAVE, then close mGBA.
Back up: open your Project Blonde folder. Copy the file with the game’s name ending in .sav into another folder. To see file endings, switch on File name extensions in File Explorer’s View menu.

Get the new version from Get the game on this page. If it comes as a patch, apply it to your base game as described there, so that you end up with a new .gba file. Put the new .gba in your Project Blonde folder, next to the old one.
Restore: mGBA matches the save by name. Make a copy of your .sav and give the copy exactly the same name as the new game file, ending in .sav instead of .gba.
In mGBA choose File → Load ROM… and open the new game.
On the title menu choose Continue.

devices.name: macOS
steps: In the game press START and choose SAVE, then quit mGBA.

Back up: open your Project Blonde folder in Finder. Copy the file with the game’s name ending in .sav into another folder. To see file endings, open Finder → Settings → Advanced and tick Show all filename extensions.

Get the new version from Get the game on this page. If it comes as a patch, apply it to your base game as described there, so that you end up with a new .gba file. Put the new .gba in your Project Blonde folder, next to the old one.
Restore: mGBA matches the save by name. Duplicate your .sav and give the copy exactly the same name as the new game file, ending in .sav instead of .gba.
In mGBA choose File → Load ROM… and open the new game.
On the title menu choose Continue.

update.check_title: Check your adventure before you save again
check: The title screen shows the new version number under PRESS START.
The title menu offers Continue, with your name, play time and Badges.
You are standing where you last saved.
Your party, and your Pokémon in the PC boxes, are all there.
Your Trainer Card shows your Badges, and your Bag and Pokédex look right.
update.check_after: All good? Save in the game once. From here on you are playing the new version; keep the backup from before the update anyway.
update.rollback_title: If something is wrong, go back
rollback: Do not save in the new version. Close the game.
Open the old game file again. It still has its own save beside it (mGBA, RetroArch) or attached to it (Delta), untouched.
If the old save was changed too, put your backup back: copy it in beside the old game with the old game’s name, or use Import Save File on the old game in Delta.
Tell us what happened on Discord, with the two version numbers and your device.
update.caveat: Saves have carried over between every build tested so far, but that is not a promise for every future version. Each release states its own save compatibility under Current release; read it before you update. A save that has been saved in a newer version may not open in an older one, which is why the backup comes first.
